category_title: Students motivated by gamification and rewards
minimal_context: The student is working independently on math problems in a computer lab using a self-paced learning platform.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please continue working on your math problems on the platform.

STUDENT: I'm trying to complete these to accumulate energy points so I can buy a more interesting avatar. It makes this really 'fun' and 'game-like'.

TUTOR: You seem to be stuck on this current problem. What do you think you should do next?

STUDENT: I'm just going to keep trying to guess the answer. I like seeing the ✔ marks build up and I need to get my five-in-a-row.

TUTOR: There is an embedded hint button on the screen that you can use.

STUDENT: No, I'm not clicking that. If I click the hint button, I automatically receive an ✗ and I won't earn points for this exercise. I don't want it to interrupt my streak and make me rebuild back towards five-in-a-row.

options.A: Allow the student to choose between response methods (e.g., dictate, oral, written, typed) for the math problems.
options.B: Deliver verbal statements or gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment.
options.C: Project the real-time data so the student can compare their own progress on the platform to their peers.
options.D: Provide math flash cards with corrective feedback and number line illustrations for the student to practice.
